title: Move a speed pourer from the empty liquor bottle to the new one: hold the bottle, draw the pourer, push it home
instruction: Move the speed pourer from the empty bottle into the new bottle.
context: When a well bottle runs dry mid-service, the bartender pulls its friction-fit speed pourer and seats it on the replacement bottle. The finned stopper grips harder than an empty bottle weighs, requiring bimanual counter-holding so the bottle is not lifted off the bar. The pourer must be aligned with the 19 mm bore and pushed past friction until its collar seats on the lip. Both bottles are 30 cm tall glass bottles standing loose on the bar counter. Occupations: bartenders (35-3011, 711,140 workers) and barbacks/helpers (35-9011, 483,390), totaling 1,194,530 US jobs (BLS OEWS May 2023). O*NET 35-3011.00 lists stocking and prepping bar supplies; every active well bottle uses a pourer.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the bar top. Nothing is powered or pressurised. Bar mat: a fixed black rubber mat 16 x 30 x 0.4 cm centred at x 27, y 0; both bottles stand on it, loose. Empty bottle at x 27, y 7: a 750 ml round glass liquor bottle, empty, 420 g, pale green; 29.5 cm tall; body 7.6 cm across and 19 cm tall; a 2.5 cm tall shoulder stepping in (five 0.5 cm steps, 7.0 to 3.6 cm across) to a 2.9 cm neck that starts 21.5 cm up; bore 1.9 cm across and 8 cm deep; a 3.4 cm bead round the neck 2.1 to 2.9 cm under the lip. New bottle at x 27, y -7: the same bottle in amber, full (1,130 g: the glass plus 750 ml of 40 % spirit), its cap already off and away. Speed pourer, seated in the empty bottle: a 35 g stainless tapered-spout pourer of the common free-flow pattern (Spill-Stop 285-50 type), 11.8 cm tall overall; below its 2.6 cm collar (0.3 cm thick) a black finned poly-cork stopper 3.2 cm long (1.6 cm core, five flexible ribbed sealing fins with outer tip diameter 21.5 mm compressing into the 19 mm bore for 2.6 cm, with an 11 mm lead for 0.6 cm); above the collar the spout, 1.3 cm across for its first 3.4 cm and 0.8 cm across for a 3.0 cm straight section plus a 2.2 cm tip bent 35 deg away from the robot. The stopper is a friction fit in either neck: 6 N to slide it in or out, more than the empty bottle's 4.1 N weight and less than the full one's 11.1 N. Round sections are regular octagons; the new bottle and the pourer have flats facing along x and y, the empty bottle is turned 22.5 deg from that. Real-world equivalent: a bartender's well station with two 750 ml liquor bottles on a bar mat, the replacement filled with water for trials, and a metal speed pourer with a finned poly stopper.
scoring: From the recorded poses. Travel: how far the pourer's collar is above the lip along the neck's axis (0 seated; 32 mm when the stopper's end is at the lip). Standing: a bottle within 8 deg of upright with its base centre over the mat and within 4 mm of its top. Out of the empty bottle: the stopper's end above that lip, or more than 9.5 mm off that neck's axis. Started in the new bottle: travel 27 mm or less (at least 5 mm of stopper in the bore), within 3.5 mm of the axis and 8 deg of it. Home: travel 2 mm or less, within 2 mm and 5 deg. Tug: once the pourer is home with both bottles standing, both gripper TCPs 2 cm clear of it and every collision piece of both arms 2 mm clear of it, and it has not moved 0.5 mm for 0.5 s, the scorer pulls the spout base straight up with 3.5 N for 0.5 s (on a real rig, a spring scale); it passes if the pourer rises 1 mm or less. Missing or non-finite pose or robot-clearance observations fail closed. Score: 0.3 the pourer out of the empty bottle and that bottle standing; 0.5 also started in the new bottle, that bottle standing; 0.7 also home; 1.0 also the tug passed, both bottles and the pourer at rest, and both arms clear (same clearances) of all three; success when held 1 s. 0, latched for the episode, if either bottle is ever more than 45 deg off upright (knocked over). Scored at the last step; possible scores 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1.0.
reset_notes: Draw the pourer out of the new bottle and seat it in the empty one, spout tip pointing away from the robot. Stand both bottles on their marks on the mat. Top the new bottle back up if any was spilt. In simulation the reset also turns each octagonal section back to its starting angle.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; round sections are octagons. The 21.5 mm fin tips compress into the 19 mm neck bore, modeled via a prismatic joint along the bore with 6 N Coulomb friction (0.5 mm elastic give) rather than mesh FEA; closes once lead is 5 mm in and in line. 6 N friction (and 3.5 N retention) matches measured commercial Spill-Stop poly-cork fits in 750 ml liquor bottles. Spirit is rigid mass, no slosh. Glass does not break; tipping over latches 0.
